title: Algebraic nearby roots over a dense subfield with explicit tolerance
statement:
Let $D\subseteq K\subseteq L$ be field inclusions [def-pc-field-extension]. Equip $K,L$ with real-valued norms satisfying $\|z\|\geq0$, $\|z\|=0\Leftrightarrow z=0$, $\|1\|=1$, $\|zw\|=\|z\|\|w\|$ and $\|z+w\|\leq\|z\|+\|w\|$, with the norm on $L$ restricting to that on $K$ and distance $d(z,w)=\|z-w\|$. Assume $L$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $D$ is dense in $K$, meaning that for every $z\in K$ and $s>0$ there is $u\in D$ with $\|z-u\|<s$. Let $f\in K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] be monic of degree $n\geq1$, let $x\in L$ satisfy $f(x)=0$ [def-weil-polynomial-root], and fix a real $r>0$. Set $M=\max\{\|x\|,1\}$ and $\varepsilon=(r/M)^n/(n+1)$. There exist a monic $g\in D[T]$ of degree $n$ and $b\in L$ such that, writing $h\in K[T]$ for the coefficientwise image of $g$, the polynomial $h$ is monic of degree $n$ and splits into linear factors in $L[T]$, $\|h_i-f_i\|<\varepsilon$ for all $i\geq0$, and
$$h(b)=g(b)=0,\qquad \|x-b\|<\big((n+1)\varepsilon\big)^{1/n}M=r.$$
Here evaluation of $g$ in $L$ uses the composite inclusion $D\to K\to L$. In particular $b$ is algebraic over $D$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]. No completeness, separability, characteristic-zero or norm on $D$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $t=r/M$. Since $M=\max\{\|x\|,1\}\geq1$ and $r>0$, we have $t>0$ and $\varepsilon=t^n/(n+1)>0$. As $n\geq1$, taking the positive real $n$th root gives $((n+1)\varepsilon)^{1/n}=(t^n)^{1/n}=t$, and hence $((n+1)\varepsilon)^{1/n}M=r$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-monic-dense-approximation] to $D\subseteq K$, the given monic $f$ and the positive $\varepsilon$ from step 1. Density is exactly its hypothesis; no norm on $D$ is needed. Obtain a monic $g\in D[T]$ of degree $n$ with $\|h_i-f_i\|<\varepsilon$ for every $i\geq0$, where $h$ is its coefficientwise image in $K[T]$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3, countability input; agent expansion of project WeilConjectures/NumberTheory/Padics/Extension.lean:110–126, using Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Approximation.lean:114–124, 132–138.

proof.text: By the coefficient description in [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $g_n=1$ and $g_i=0$ for $i>n$. Each inclusion sends these coefficients to $1$ and $0$. Thus $h$, and its coefficientwise image $q\in L[T]$, are nonzero monic polynomials of degree $n$. Apply [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] to $q$: its leading coefficient is $1$, so $q=\prod_{j=1}^{m}(T-\gamma_j)$. Multiplying these monic linear factors gives coefficient $1$ at $T^m$ and zero above $m$, so comparison with $\deg q=n$ gives $m=n$. Thus $h$ splits into $n$ linear factors over $L$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3, countability input; agent expansion of project WeilConjectures/NumberTheory/Padics/Extension.lean:110–126, using Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Approximation.lean:114–124, 132–138.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-roots-coefficient-proximity] to the normed extension $L/K$, polynomials $f,h$, root $x$ and tolerance $\varepsilon$. The norms restrict as required; $f,h$ are monic of the same positive degree $n$, all coefficient inequalities hold by step 2, and $h$ splits by step 3. It gives $b\in L$ with $h(b)=0$ and $\|x-b\|<((n+1)\varepsilon)^{1/n}M=r$ by step 1.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3, countability input; agent expansion of project WeilConjectures/NumberTheory/Padics/Extension.lean:110–126, using Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Approximation.lean:114–124, 132–138.

proof.text: Write the inclusions as $\iota:D\to K$ and $\jmath:K\to L$. The evaluation formula of [def-weil-polynomial-root] gives $h(b)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}\jmath(\iota(g_i))b^i=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(\jmath\circ\iota)(g_i)b^i=g(b)$. Hence $g(b)=0$ for the specified composite inclusion. Since $g_n=1\ne0$, the polynomial $g$ is nonzero, and [def-weil-algebraic-element] says precisely that this makes $b$ algebraic over $D$. Together with steps 2–4 this gives every asserted clause.
